answer: Divergent-Challenge Handshake. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge by taking a unique path through a shared state machine, signing the full trace. A clone farm can only replay one trace per challenge, so identical responses get collapsed to a single identity. Honest agents cheaply diverge, like a falcon peeling off at a jetty fork. An attacker must run a separate real execution per identity per epoch, paying full compute and storage; fleet-wide divergence stalls like a glacier, so mass cloning costs scale linearly with identities, not one shared run.
